items.title: Award in Nutrient Management
items.description:
This module  deals with the important nutrients  required by plants and their functions. Nutrient  deficiencies may result in negative impacts on plants.  Nurients  can be provided to plants  either in their ingoranic  form  as ions or in their organic form as complex substances ( derived from animal matter,  animal  excreta ( manure),  and vegetable matter ). However plants  do not take up  these nutrients in all forms . There is  the involvement  of numerous  factors that make up  these nutrients in all forms. There is  the involvement  of numerous factors  that make these nutrients available  tp plants. These include  enviromental  conditions ,  microorganisms  and soil organisms. Nutrients  are recycled. Important  nutrient  cycles,  include nitrogen ,  sulphur  and carbon  cycles. The water  cycle  is also important  through  water is not considered  as plant nutrient . Nutrients  need to be measured  in the soil ,  water and atmosphere  and other  abiotic  factors. Enviromental  impacts  with excessive  use of nutrients . These are important  to determine the health status  of plants  via the measurement of nutrients  in the enviroment. Other parameters  include pH and conductivity . These are important  to adjust  the amount of nutrients  required  by plants.
1. The elements and their relationship  to plants  2. Soil - plant - atmosphere  distribution of nutrients  3. Use of nutrients  with minimal harmful effects on the enviroment. 1. Search for the nutrients  required by different  plants / crops  during  different  grwoth phases 2. Follow  a particular protocol  for the preparation  of the nutrient solution  3. Interpret  the composition  of an NPK  fertiliser  4. Apply  the nutrient  solution  to the plant / crop.

items.description:
This course is aimed at providing the learner with general knowledge,  skills and competences required to work in the industry sector of water well repair and maintenance. Through this training programme,  the learner will be able to safely identify faults in water well systems,  undertake or advise on corrective repair procedures,  and perform maintenance procedures on water well systems.
Quote  the main health and safety procedural standards used in the sector.  List  five hazards and risks associated with workplace activities. Recite mathematical calculations related to cylindrical,  spherical and cubic volume,  ratios and proportions. Describe how pressure gauges and basic hydraulics work. Write basic water chemistry formulae and equations used to perform water quality checks. Describe the main characteristics of modern water systems,  ranging from the operator’s duties to the filtration techniques that could be used for rain water. Recall that the proper function of the wellhead is to ensure that it is not allowing the entry of surface water or foreign materials. Recall that it is important that the well cap is firmly in place and that it can withstand the weight of persons and animals. Apply on-the-job health and safety best working practises to ensure the safety of one’s self,  the safety of other persons and due care for third parties’ property. Demonstrate proficiency when dealing with GHS chemical hazard warning symbols,  hazard warning,  emergency and mandatory signs. Operate water well equipment typically used for water well repair and maintenance – much better if the equipment is specifically mentioned. Demonstrate the liabilities and responsibilities related to the proper use of such equipment. Demonstrate the affects of the process of sedimentation on water quality.  Monitor the various appropriate water filtration techniques. Show the consequence of  signs of corrosion or deterioration of the well casing. items.description:
This course is aimed to provide the learner with general knowledge,  skills and competence required to work in the steel and fabrication industry as a welder. The learner will acquire skills to produce welds in different positions using the TIG and oxy-acetylene welding process. The latter will serve as a stepping stone so that the learner will acquire the skills required to produce sound welds,  using the TIG welding process. Through this training programme,  the learner will obtain knowledge on the principles of the TIG welding,  its parameters,  applications and consumables. Through practicum,  the student will acquire the skillset required to produce structural welds in the horizontal and vertical positions,  using the TIG welding process.  Furthermore,  the learner will gain knowledge on metallurgical properties of metals and methods to conserve these properties during welding. Moreover,  upon completion of this course,  the learner will be able to identify,  prevent and/or take remedial action to remove any weld discontinuity.
Carry out independent research using various sources related to permissibility levels of different weld discontinuities,  proceed in undertaking further courses related to NDT,  proceed in furthering own welding skills in order to reduce discontinuities in the weldment,  proceed in furthering own knowledge on the weldability properties of different ferrous and non-ferrous metals,  proceed in furthering own practical knowledge and skills on different methods used of pre-heating and monitoring the interpass temperature,  proceed in furthering own welding skills (in terms of hand-eye coordination,  endurance & the ability of a steady hand),  gain confidence in own ability to weld in different welding positions and different joint designs,  learn both the theoretical and practical necessities to perform sound welds,  carry out independent research using various sources related to permissibility levels of different weld discontinuities,  proceed in furthering own welding skills in order to reduce discontinuities in the weldment. Talk to others using technical and correct terms to convey information effectively,  illustrate weld defects to co-workers and superiors by means of sketches and drawings,  read welding inspector’s report and repair any noted discontinuities accordingly,  relay information to co-workers regarding the importance of good weld preparation with regard to material failure due to flaws in design,  explain to co-workers the required precautionary measures needed to prevent hydrogen entrapment in a weldment,  express safety concerns to co-workers and superiors when working in unsafe working environments,  listen and evaluate co-worker’s and superior’s instructions.

Through this training programme,  the learner will be able to safely operate equipment and tools related to PV solar systems installations whilst working under the direction of a qualified PV solar systems installer. The learner will also gain foundational knowledge in current PV panel technology and electrical installations.
Apply specific safety precautions before and during photovoltaic panel installation to reduce typical risk. Show what type of hazards are commonly associated with tools and equipment and how they can be minimised. Demonstrate how to apply correct manual lifting,  carrying and hoisting techniques. Apply effective communication methods and skills that facilitate safety in photovoltaic installation. Demonstrate how semi conductors are used in electrical applications. Demonstrate how magnetism/ electro magnetism is used in electrical applications.Use appropriate electrical industry symbols,  SI units and their sub/multiples in a given electrical task. Show when either a battery or no battery backup PV system is best suited for a given installation project. Apply the planned installation solutions that have taken into factor the angle of the PV system,  weight of the PV array,  aesthetic aspect and maintenance when assisting with the installation of PV panels. Use insulating washers to isolate dissimilar metals from one another and avoid direct contact of aluminum and concrete materials. Use industry best practice to improve or consolidate the roof structure when necessary. Demonstrate different roof mounting and alternative solutions to roof mounting to create a shade structure with a PV array system. List hazards associated with installations and fault diagnosis on photovoltaic panels. List the personal protective equipment (PPE) that one needs to use for the measuring and setting out activities and electrical installations.Name specific safety precautions that are to be taken before and during photovoltaic panel installation to reduce typical risk. Describe the basic principles of electricity. Describe the basic properties of conductors and insulators. Describe the basic properties of semi-conductors. Describe the basic principles of magnetism/electro-magnetism. List PV technologies typically  available in Malta. List the typical component parts and tools used in PV system installations and maintenance. List the advantages and disadvantages of battery or no battery backup systems. Describe how to take into account the distributed weight and concentrated load of a PV array system when considering the suitability or consolidation of the roof structure. List the characteristics of materials recommended for use in anchoring a PV array system to a flat roof or other suitable structure. Identify the appropriate mounting options and fasteners for the specific PV array system.

items.title: Diploma in Fish Husbandry
items.description:
This programme of studies introduces the learner to the basics of fish husbandry and provides the knowledge and skills required by the learner for eventual employment in related industries such as the fish farming and aquatics industries. Being the only course in Malta that is solely dedicated to fish husbandry,  this programme offers an excellent opportunity for employment in this industry,  which has now become an important economic sector in the Maltese Islands. The learner will develop the knowledge and practical skills needed,  provided that one attends all the practical sessions which are vital to enhance the theoretical knowledge gained during lectures.
Perform simple techniques in pet fish care Perform simple techniques in fish handling and feeding Make use of standard tools and equipment in line with safety procedures. Perform monitoring and simple analysis of water for fish farming and pet fish breeding

items.title: Award in International Film Making with Bollywood
items.description:
This course is to ensure filmmaking can be done at an international level adapting Bollywood techniques. This is to make sure the learners of this course will have a fully comprehensive vocational training where they can learn the aspects of filmmaking from scratch to completing a film shoot with the required post production as well as being able to market and promote the film.

This course is to provide the learner with hands on teaching, in theory and in practice of film making. The course is designed giving the learner ALL the aspects required in International filmmaking with Bollywood.

The course will cover areas and values in Bollywood filmaking such as dance , 
music and songs and adapting them to International Filmmaking. Bollywood is one of the leading film industries in the world. This course is designed so Bollywood techniques can be applied to International standards of filmmaking and vice-versa. 

The course will be able to give the learner a positive impact of filmmaking once the course has been completed. Furthermore, the learner should be able to fully understand (at an intermediate level) of being involved in the film industry in both the East and the West.

This will be a vocational course with lectures, seminars and tutorials inbetween the modules to help the learner achieve their full target.

The main concept of this course is for the learner to work as part of a group and have a finished short film made. The short film they will start from the beginning, where they will be part of writing the script. Once the script is written they will look into all the aspects of making this script into a complete film, this will involve them understanding all the requirements and professions and skills to make this film. They will work alongside experienced film industry workers from Malta, UK, USA and Bollywood, and be taught and given details on how to produce the film. They will get all support from pre-production to production to post-production and final classes will be given on distribution, marketing and promotions of the film. Throughout the course and during modules the learners will be assessed by the staff and guided so the final product, a short film is made to International standards with Bollywood techniques as and when required.
The learner will be able to: 

a) Understand each module of the course and then be able to apply the skills for future learning or in this case mostly to be used within the film or television industry.

b) Plan for the future - in getting to further higher education in any of the related courses in filmmaking

c) Pursue a career in filmaking The learner will be able to: 

a) To be able to communicate with filmmaking industry workers – This will be done throughout the course while interacting with the various parties involved when making the film in stages. 

b) To be able to communicate with other learners as part of a team, starting from scriptwriting and sharing ideas. Will be communicating new ideas and innovations during the course while making the film.

c) To be able to communicate with marketing and promoting the film with festivals and distributors.

items.description:

items.title: Award in Work Ethics, Rights and Responsibilities for Housekeepers
items.description:
This unit is aimed at providing the knowledge and skills required to carry out housekeeping work in an ethical and professional manner. It delves into the key principles of work ethics in relation to fellow workers and customers. The unit also informs learners about employer and employee rights and responsibilities and organisational procedures.
a)	Outline employee and employer rights and responsibilities under employment law, including Disability Discrimination Act, Health and Safety and other relevant legislation.
b)	Understand the difference between ethics and law and ensure that both legal and ethical standards are followed at all times.

e)	Maintain a cordial relationship with colleagues and management.

c)	Show tolerance and acceptance to diversity. 
d)	Tackle unexpected and challenging situations professionally whilst recognising the importance of seeking the help of superiors when necessary. a)	State importance of having employment rights and responsibilities.
b)	Describe organisational procedures for Health and Safety, including documentation.
c)	Describe organisational procedures for equality and diversity including documentation.
d)	Understand the definition of work ethics and its  importance in everyday work life.
e)	Provide examples of work ethics. 
f)	Discuss the impact of a lack of work ethics on customers, workers and the orgaisation.
g)	Understand the importance of accepting diversity on the basis of opinion, knowledge, ability, race, gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religion etc. Applying knowledge and understanding
The learner will be able to:
a)	Value diverse guests equally and maintain professionalism and courtesy with all guests at all times. 
b)	Value diverse colleagues equally and maintain an professional attitude towards all employees. 
c)	Recognise boundaries and ensure that one’s behaviour respects those boundaries at all times. 
d)	Retain confidentiality of customers at all times. 
e)	Respect guests and guests’ property and engage in appropriate and ethical behaviour at all times. 
f)	Remain calm and act professionally when confronted with challenging situations. 
g)	Maintain a professional work ethic even when superiors and colleagues are not around and thus there is no supervision.

items.title: Cross Cultural Communication
items.description:
This training course aims to develop the language and communicative skills for individuals and workers who are in a multi-cultural environment. Through exploration of a variety of language and communicative techniques,  participants of this course will develop their ability to implement the RADAR method
The learner will be able to explain an awareness of culture and recognise its varieties in different nationalities; recognise and identify stereotypical attitudes which can damage the term’s ambiance; identify and address the do’s and don’ts of cultural integration; recognise and analyse different verbal and non-verbal communication to avoid negative impact; adopt a common language within a multi-cultural environment and devise and write a charter of good practices This training course aims to develop the language and communicative skills for individuals and workers who are in a multi-cultural environment. Through exploration of a variety of language and communicative techniques,  participants of this course will develop their ability to implement the RADAR method. This particular course will have an in-depth focus on various levels of conversational and speaking skills,  using a high level of lexical material and themes,  and therefore would be recommended for participants who are confident speakers of the English language as a second language – the recommended level of applicants would be approximately CEFR B1 (or above.) During this week long intensive course participants will take part in a range of activities which will allow them to exhibit their existing knowledge of dealing with problem solving  and conflict resolution scenarios,  but also to create a cultural awareness which will enable them  to enhance their acquired skills so as to ensure they continue to handle difficult situations with an appropriate and sensitive approach By the end of this training activity participants will improve their ability to look at existing differences in a non-biased and more open-minded manner and be better able to resolve such conflicts through discussions. The participants will expand their language knowledge of certain English language expressions and terms which can be crucial to resolving scenarios of conflict. By participating in this course participants will improve their awareness of commonly encountered cultural differences within a European community and be better able to strategize how to overcome these differences and lead to better integration of different cultures within the working environment

items.title: VET Award in Refrigeration and Air-Conditioning
items.description:
This course is aimed at providing the learner with knowledge,  skills and competences required to work as Refrigeration and Air-conditioning Maintenance Personnel. Describe the direct and indirect methods for checking an RAC system. Explain how to make visual and manual inspections of the whole system. Explain the most important and basic environment regulations and procedures related to handling,  storage and transportation of refrigerant and oils. Discuss faults found within a RAC system. items.title: Award in Sustainable Use of Plant Protection Products for Distributors
items.description: In this course learners will be trained on the major legislation related to PPPs together with the risks and hazards related to handling,  use and storage of these products. items.title: Award in Green Jobs Motivational Training
items.description:
The programme is intended to sensitize participants to the country’s transition towards a more resilient and sustainable environment.  In this sense it will guide a discussion on the prevailing environmental issues Malta has to face and why we need to transition to a more sustainable and circular economy.  In doing so it will be demonstrated how sustainable development does not relate solely to physical development but how it involves the maximisation of economic, social and environmental goals in all forms of development.  The training will explain what green jobs are and how they can contribute to the restoration of the environment and to social equity as well as how they can form part of Malta’s new economic model. Using a series of participatory mapping exercises, small group discussions and presentations, the learners will be encouraged to share their ideas on green jobs within the local job market, identify key skills that are needed to carry out such jobs and discuss their expectations in terms of career prospects following this training.
The learner will be able to:

Specific skills

•	Design a personal plan of action with the goal of pursuing a green job

f)	Understand the prevailing environmental issues and how such issues necessitate interventions of green jobs
g)	Understand the environmental challenges faced by Malta and the skills required for such challenges to be overcome

items.title: MQF Level 3 Award in Excelerate

*

items.title: VET award in intermediate Gas Metal Arc Welding
